INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — TERMLY EXAM #9 (TERM 3)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which is an interjection? (1 mark)
   A. Table
   B. Beside
   C. Quickly
   D. Hurray!

2. Which interjection fits a small mistake? (1 mark)
   A. Hurray
   B. Oops
   C. Wow
   D. Bravo

3. What is a good way to learn interjections in your mother tongue? (1 mark)
   A. Listen to elders and ask when they are used
   B. Guess meanings
   C. Invent them
   D. Ignore them

4. Which is NOT a feeling shown by interjections? (1 mark)
   A. Joy
   B. The price of an item
   C. Pain
   D. Disgust

5. A good dialogue should have (1 mark)
   A. no characters
   B. an ending
   C. only one word
   D. no words

6. What is a dialogue? (1 mark)
   A. A map
   B. A conversation between two or more people
   C. A list
   D. A long description

7. What is a digital device? (1 mark)
   A. A machine that works with electronic signals to help us communicate or work
   B. A type of song
   C. A wooden tool
   D. A kind of fruit

8. Which is the last part of a telephone conversation? (1 mark)
   A. Asking for a favour
   B. Greeting
   C. Giving your name
   D. Saying goodbye

9. Why do we match devices to their uses? (1 mark)
   A. To know what each is for
   B. To lose them
   C. To hide them
   D. To break them

10. What does the lead of a news item give? (1 mark)
   A. The main facts
   B. A poem
   C. A joke
   D. The ending

11. What is a quote in news? (1 mark)
   A. A price
   B. A map
   C. The exact words of a person
   D. A drawing

12. Why should you write true information on a form? (1 mark)
   A. False answers are best
   B. Nobody reads forms
   C. Forms are records and false information causes problems
   D. It is a game

13. What does N/A mean? (1 mark)
   A. Next assignment
   B. New address
   C. Not applicable
   D. No answer always

14. Which word in The teacher counted the votes is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. teacher
   B. votes
   C. counted
   D. the

15. Which is a polite phrase for asking someone to explain again? (1 mark)
   A. Never mind
   B. Say it again now
   C. Pardon me, could you explain?
   D. You are silly

16. What is rhythm? (1 mark)
   A. The page number
   B. The title
   C. The ink
   D. The beat or flow when a poem is read aloud

17. What is the message of a poem? (1 mark)
   A. The main idea the poet wants to share
   B. The number of lines
   C. The date
   D. The printer

18. Why should instruction charts use large clear letters? (1 mark)
   A. To make them heavy
   B. So people can read them from a distance
   C. To use more ink
   D. To hide meaning

19. What does a red eight-sided road sign tell drivers? (1 mark)
   A. Go faster
   B. Park
   C. Stop
   D. Turn left

20. Which is a verb in Open your book? (1 mark)
   A. your
   B. the
   C. book
   D. Open

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Describe the steps for creating a form for your class about favourite cultural foods. (5 marks)

22. Compose a four-line poem about a good leader. Make lines two and four rhyme. (4 marks)

23. Explain why clear instructions are important on a road. (3 marks)

24. Write a four-line dialogue between two friends deciding what to do in their free time. Use two interjections. (4 marks)

25. Write two polite phrases to interrupt. (2 marks)

26. List three polite expressions used during a telephone call. (3 marks)

27. Explain what an instruction chart is. (2 marks)

28. Match each interjection with its feeling: (a) Hurray (b) Yuck. (2 marks)

29. State three steps for writing a dialogue. (3 marks)

30. Name two digital devices and give a use of each. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — TERMLY EXAM #9 (TERM 3) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — Hurray!
   Hurray shows joy.

2. B — Oops
   Oops shows a small mistake.

3. A — Listen to elders and ask when they are used
   Learning from speakers is reliable.

4. B — The price of an item
   Interjections show feelings, not prices.

5. B — an ending
   Every piece needs an ending.

6. B — A conversation between two or more people
   A dialogue is people talking.

7. A — A machine that works with electronic signals to help us communicate or work
   Phones and computers are digital devices.

8. D — Saying goodbye
   Calls end with a goodbye.

9. A — To know what each is for
   Knowing the use helps us choose the right device.

10. A — The main facts
   The lead gives the key facts.

11. C — The exact words of a person
   A quote repeats what someone said.

12. C — Forms are records and false information causes problems
   Honest answers are important.

13. C — Not applicable
   N/A means the question does not apply.

14. C — counted
   Counted shows the action.

15. C — Pardon me, could you explain?
   Pardon me and could you are polite.

16. D — The beat or flow when a poem is read aloud
   Rhythm is the pattern of sounds.

17. A — The main idea the poet wants to share
   The message is the main idea.

18. B — So people can read them from a distance
   Clarity helps readers.

19. C — Stop
   That shape is the stop sign.

20. D — Open
   Open is the action.

SECTION B
----
21. (5 marks)
   Answer: Decide the purpose, write a title, list questions such as name, class and favourite food, leave space for answers, write short instructions, test it with a friend and improve it.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each step up to five.

22. (4 marks)
   Answer: Any four-line poem on leadership with two rhyming lines, for example A good leader listens, Speaks the truth each day, Helps the weak and lonely, And shows the proper way.
   Working / marking points: Two marks for theme and four lines, two marks for rhyme.

23. (3 marks)
   Answer: Clear road instructions and signs tell drivers and walkers what to do, which prevents accidents and keeps everyone safe.
   Working / marking points: One mark for telling what to do, one for preventing accidents, one for safety.

24. (4 marks)
   Answer: Any four lines with speaker names, colons, a clear topic and two suitable interjections.
   Working / marking points: One mark for names and colons, one mark for suitable content, one mark for each interjection.

25. (2 marks)
   Answer: Excuse me, may I say something? Sorry to interrupt, but could you repeat that?
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

26. (3 marks)
   Answer: Good morning, please, thank you, excuse me, goodbye, may I speak to (any three).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

27. (2 marks)
   Answer: An instruction chart is a poster that shows the steps of a task in order using short words and often pictures.
   Working / marking points: One mark for steps in order and one for a poster or pictures.

28. (2 marks)
   Answer: (a) joy (b) disgust
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

29. (3 marks)
   Answer: Choose theme, choose characters, decide setting, write each speaker on a new line, use interjections, read aloud.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each step.

30. (2 marks)
   Answer: Phone for calling, radio for hearing news, camera for taking photos (any two with uses).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each device with its use.
